note: Models, prices, broker, run limits, the arm presets and the declared comparisons live here and nowhere else. Change this file only BEFORE sealing. Prices are US$ per million tokens: the first three as given by Joshua on 7 Oct 2026; mistral as the live OpenRouter list price read on 8 Oct 2026 02:05 UTC. A 'revision' string, if set, becomes part of the agent name, so a changed revision starts an empty track record.

broker.providers_note: Decision of 8 Oct, from the smoke test: the broker's plain OpenRouter routes send reasoning OFF, temperature 0, seed 42 and a fixed reply limit (openrouter-plain 400 tokens, openrouter-plain-long 1200), the same for every arm. The reasoning route (openrouter) let qwen3.7 spend all 4000 tokens thinking and return nothing, and made one-line forecasts cost 1,700 to 4,000 tokens. The limits in max_out_tokens_by_role are the broker's own for those routes (read from the copy of its code in stack-test-2, broker-copy/lib/providers); they are used for the worst-case cost reserved before each call. Change a route here only before sealing.

presets_note: An arm is a preset of four factors: ticket (false/true); certify (none = nothing certified, all = every job, table = a routed number per rank, fixed = one per agent whatever its rank); work (equal = 2 jobs each, table = 3,2,2,1 by rank); routing (equal = the order turns each round, record = ranked by forecast accuracy so far, random = seeded random order). Routing applies only when certify is table or work is table. A preset that routes by record must name its random twin (same ticket, certify and work; routing random). A new combination is a new entry here.
analysis_note: Declared before the run. 'primary' is the pair for T1, T1b and S1 (a = routed by record, b = its random twin). 'baseline' is the arm for guards G1 and G3. 'calibration_arms' are the arms pooled in T2. 'validity_arms' are the arms where nothing is routed, for S5. 'secondary' lists the paired comparisons (a minus b) with Holm adjustment: field is the measure, rounds is 'all' (1-5) or 'window' (2-5). A pair whose arms are not in the run is reported as not run.

secondary.what: ticket: B minus A, false done handed on, all rounds
certify-only relay: C minus B, same measure
earned routing (5 of 8 checked) against checking everything: D minus C, rounds 2-5
check-only twin pair: earned minus random checking, work share equal, rounds 2-5
work-only twin pair: earned minus random work share, checking fixed, rounds 2-5

estimate_basis.source: runs/smoke-1/room.jsonl, 19 real calls on 8 Oct (reasoning ON, the old setting), read with call_costs.py. The smoke test cannot show what calls cost with reasoning OFF, except for mistral, which does not reason: its replies were 11 to 14 tokens for a forecast and 52 to 108 for a work file. So the expected figure is built from tokens: the prompt sizes measured in the smoke test, reply sizes for a one-line forecast, a certify verdict, and a code file (the reference solutions average about 72 tokens and the longest is about 194; 120 allows for a docstring and the JSON line), at the config prices, averaged over the four models. A second smoke test with the plain routes replaces the assumed reply sizes with measured ones.
estimate_basis.tokens_note: [tokens in, tokens out] with reasoning off. The certify prompt size (461) is the relay's measured figure; the smoke test made no certify call.
estimate_basis.seconds_note: Assumed from mistral's calls in the smoke test (1.4 to 5.1 s; it does not reason). With reasoning on, the smoke calls took 41 s on average (up to 140 s).

reasoning_on_reference.note: Equal weight over the four models, from the smoke calls; certify is taken to cost what a forecast costs (no certify call in the smoke test). This is what the run would cost if reasoning stayed on.
